Simplest model: time ≈ fixed (~0.15–0.25 s, partly removable) + steps × per-step cost. Per-step cost is pixel-proportional plus a large memory-bound component on the 31×31 maps (whitening output and group 1: BN/GELU/pool). Accuracy rises slowly with total steps, about 0.2 pp per 0.5 epoch, costing roughly 1.5–2.7 s/pp.

Results I missed: the freeze saves more than I predicted. E028 saved about 0.5 s and E034 reached 5.48 s versus my 5.72 s. E031 (sample dropping) and E026 (early 20 px) also beat every range. Accuracy misses in the other direction: E025, E030 and E032 all cost 0.3–0.7 pp. Averaging and LS tweaks sit at an optimum and tend to hurt.

Mechanisms:
1. Early low resolution is cheap (E026, E033). The 32 px tail and the 3×3 final-map regime carry accuracy (E011, E018, E024).
2. Memory-bound cuts save more than their MAC share (E028, E034). The annealed group-1 LR makes the freeze nearly free in accuracy. Group-1 and whitening backward is the main lever. Deeper freeze, BN folding and whitening-bias stop are the same family with diminishing returns.
3. Averaging, LS and warmup tweaks (E025, E029, E030, E032) are null or negative.
4. wd ×0.5 helped about 0.2 pp (E016). Muon's gain is confounded with batch size and an RNG re-draw (E006).
5. Systems work is worth about 1% each (CUDA graphs E015, prepare cost E035). E035's math-identical change stayed within noise on accuracy and saved about 0.03 s.

Noise: 3-seed accuracy SE is about 0.1–0.15 pp. Held-out 10-seed SE is about 0.06 pp. Time noise is about ±0.03 s. Any RNG change re-rolls seeds 0–2. Selection on seeds 3–12 carries a winner's curse of about 0.05–0.1 pp.

The tip sits at 0.7548 on seeds 0–2, with held-out probably near 0.753, so there is almost no headroom. Further time cuts need an accuracy lever first, or must be math-neutral.

Unsure: whether the held-out mean is above 0.752; PCIe transfer of the memory-bound levers; how deep the freeze can go (60%); whether the whitening bias already stops early. In the code it is trained for 3 epochs of 9.25, about 32% of steps, so it is not stopped by 20%.

forecasts.reason: Whitening bias trains for 3 epochs (~32% of steps), so the idea applies. The saving is small (~1–2%) and well within noise.
The freeze saving scales up, but accuracy lands at or below the bar, so the keep gate is marginal.
A diagnostic with no recipe change. The fresh-seed mean is likely about 0.753 with a small winner's-curse shrink.
It removes BN reductions on the large maps for a likely 1–3% saving. Folding adds complexity and a risk of accuracy drift.
A profiling diagnostic will likely show non-GEMM kernels taking ≥30% of the step and the stem taking more than its MAC share.
Muon likely helps by 0.2–0.5 pp. Dropping it saves a little Newton-Schulz time but loses accuracy.

cruxes: Is the tip's true population mean (fresh seeds 13–22) at or above 0.752? If not, every further time trim needs an accuracy lever first.
What share of a 32 px step is group 1 plus whitening, and are non-GEMM kernels at least 30% of GPU time (H6.3.1)? This sets the value of the deeper freeze, BN folding and whitening-bias stop.
Does the whitening bias really train for about 32% of steps (3 epochs of 9.25)? If so, I054 is live but worth only about 1–2%.
